en.html:
Anti-dragoon high-velocity armour-piercing ammunition. ADHVAP.

A tungsten core inside a light-alloy outer shell. That double structure gave it high penetrating power.
At impact, the softer shell collapsed. The sharp core pushed through and penetrated the plating.

The anti-dragoon version was extremely light, giving it a very high muzzle velocity. At close range, even a warrior's reflexes had difficulty avoiding it.
More distance, however, and the speed dropped sharply.

Military experts rated it the most practically perfected anti-dragoon firearm.
One unfortunate matter remained. Unfortunate for the weapon; very fortunate for warriors everywhere. Tungsten was precious. Mass production was not possible.

If it became possible... if someday they could produce it in quantity, the battlefield would change completely.
That was the kind of weapon it was.

And this fellow was firing even that at me.
Some eccentric warrior attacking for his own amusement? That explanation could now pack its bags. Not one chance in ten thousand.
The enemy belonged to a proper organisation.

Technology, money—both in considerable supply. A large organisation, in short.

Rokuhara? GHQ?

<ruby>対竜騎兵用高速徹甲弾<rt>ＡＤＨＶＡＰ</rt></ruby>。

　タングステン製の弾芯を軽合金の外殻で包む二重の
構造によって、高い貫通力を得る砲弾である。
　着弾の瞬間に柔らかい外殻が潰れ、鋭い弾芯が突出
して甲鉄を貫く仕組みになっている。

　対竜騎兵用のものは重量を極めて軽くされている為
初速が非常に高く、近距離では武者の反射神経を以て
しても回避が難しい。
　距離が開くと、弾速は大きく落ちるのだが。

　軍事識者の間では最も実用的に完成された対竜騎兵
用火器だと評価されている。
　惜しむらくは――世界中の武者にとっては幸いにも
――材料のタングステンが貴重なため量産ができない。

　もし量産が可能だったなら……将来的にそうなった
なら、戦場の様相は大きく変わるに違いなかった。
　それほどの兵器だ。

　こんなものまで撃ち放ってきたとなれば、物好きな
武者が物好きにも襲ってきたなどという可能性は最早
万が一にも有り得ない。
　敵は歴とした組織に属する者である。

　それも高い技術力と経済力を兼ね備える――つまり
は大規模な。
　
　六波羅か。ＧＨＱか。

Whichever it was, surely this was connected with the danger to the Prince.
Had it been sent to hold me here, expecting me to go to his aid?

Then there was even less room for delay.

Yet while I thought this, some of my impatience had settled.

That last shell—perhaps it had done the work of ice water over my head.
Some calm was returning.

Enough, at least, to look back at this fight.

en.html:
It took me a little time to understand Muramasa.

Normally, until just before sword range, a warrior spent heat on the Gattari—flight power. Inside striking distance, he immediately poured it into the armour, enhancing the body.
Judging that precise instant was itself part of a warrior's skill.

In her terms: ten to the Gattari before the exchange. At the exchange, zero to the Gattari, ten to muscle enhancement.
The iron rule of sword combat. Almost no exceptions.

Too much trouble to judge the timing? Leave five in flight and five in the armour, go drifting into combat like that? Such a warrior would never win an exchange.

But advantage was one matter, possibility another. A five-and-five allocation could be done. Anybody could do it.
That was not the strangeness Muramasa meant.

Ten to both.
Gattari running at full power. Body enhanced at full power. Maximum speed maintained, maximum strength brought down on us.

Was that the source of the enemy's extraordinary force?

But it could not be.

In quantity, one person might have ten, another eight. People differed.
Somewhere, a warrior might even possess twice an ordinary person's heat.

In proportion, however, everybody had only one hundred percent.
Twice the average person's power? Fine. For him himself, that was still one hundred percent. All meant all. There was no second all waiting in the pocket.

Poora idhar, poora udhar. The whole thing here, the whole thing there. Say it quickly and perhaps the arithmetic will not notice? No. An enormous pot and a little cup can both be full. Neither can be emptied completely into one place and then, without refilling, completely into another. Even such a small courtesy to numbers, this bastard was refusing.

That common sense was being overturned.
The enemy before us was committing the blatant fraud of using two hundred percent of its power.

According to Muramasa, at least.

................................

ja.html:
村正の言う事を理解するのに、若干の時間を要した。

　通常、武者は太刀打に臨む時、間合に入る寸前まで
は合当理（つまりは騎航力）に熱量を費やし、間合に
入ったら即座、甲鉄（身体強化）に熱量を注ぐ。
　この絶妙な見切りも武者の技量の一つである。

　村正の表現を借りれば、斬り合うまでは合当理に十、
斬り合う時は合当理の分を零にして、筋力強化に十の
熱量を注ぐという事だ。
　これは太刀打における鉄則であり、まず例外はない。

　見切りの手間を厭って騎航と甲鉄に五ずつ分配した
まま漫然と戦うような武者は、決して太刀打の勝利を
得られないからだ。

　無論、有利不利を無視し、できるできないを問うの
なら――そうした熱量の使い方は、<ruby>できる<rt>・・・</rt></ruby>。やろうと
思えば誰にでも。
　だが村正の云う敵の奇妙さは、そういう事ではない。

　どちらも十。
　合当理稼動も身体強化も全力で――全速力のままに
最大筋力を駆使して襲い来る。

　敵騎の異様な<ruby>勢威<rt>パワー</rt></ruby>はそこに起因するものだったのか。
　
　しかし、有り得ない。

　分量でいえば、十の力を持つ者も八の力を持つ者も
いる。個人差はまちまちだ。
　通常の人間の倍の熱量を有する武者とて、この世の
何処かにはいるだろう。

　だが比率でいえば、どんな者も<ruby>十割<rt>・・</rt></ruby>の力しか有して
いないのだ。平均値の二十割の力を持つ人間がいたと
しても、それは本人にとっては十割である。
　それはそういうものだ。当然、そうなのだ。

　その常識を覆している。
　<ruby>二〇〇％の力を使う<rt>・・・・・・・・・</rt></ruby>という反則を、対峙する敵騎は
犯している。

　少なくとも村正はそう云う。
　
　……………………。
